main_text.p: ab altero fit nimis remotum, contigit animal in sentiendo aberrare. Unde procul difsita, aut plane non, aut minora apparent, quàm revera sunt: 2. Ut sensile justam habeat magnitudinem. Si enim nimis sit minutum & parvum, sentiri non potest. 3. Ut sit-tum justum habeat, modoque convenienteque sensorio objiciatur. Hinc animal non videt objectum præsens, nisi secundum rectam lineam oculis occurrat. 4. Ut justo tempore commoretur ante sensorium. Si enim subito & quasi in momento prætervolat sensorium, rectè sensu dijudicari non potest. 5. Ut mediocriter seu non nimis vehementer sensorium afficiat. Hinc solem oculis intentis directè non possumus intueri. 6. Ut sensile per se suam speciem ad sensorium transmittat. Hinc stellas interdum non videmus, quia à majore Solis lumine radii earum obscurantur, ut ad oculos nostros pervenire non possint.
Altera conditio concernit sensorium, & vult, ut illud sit rectè, & secundum naturam dispositum, h. e. sanum, vigens, integrum, illæsum & quietum,

page.notes: Printed page number reads "27" followed by a small mark, rendered here as 275; the right-hand page number is partly faded and read as "5i" ("Si" in the scan), so it is uncertain. The running head is "CAPVT XXI." with the chapter number partly obscured. Marginal "11." beside the second paragraph is a faint marginal mark, read with doubt. Printed ligatures and long-s forms were normalised to plain s. The first paragraph is continued from the previous page; the second paragraph starts with a large initial "A" partly obscured.
